# MDL405 · `plaintext-password`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

The file holds a password in plain text.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | options |
| Default severity | warning |
| Fix | — |
| Design references | F3 |

## Why

Configuration files are often versioned, copied between hosts and readable by more people than the database account they unlock. Keep the password out of them: put it in a separate file readable only by the backup user (passed with `--defaults-extra-file`), or let your secret manager provide it at run time.

## Example

❌ Before:

```ini
[client]
user=backup
password=s3cret
[mydumper]
password=x
```

```text
3:10-3:16 warning MDL405[plaintext-password] password in plain text
  = Anyone who can read this file, or its history in version control, can connect to the server as this user.
5:10-5:11 warning MDL405[plaintext-password] password in plain text
  = Anyone who can read this file, or its history in version control, can connect to the server as this user.
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL405: warning   # or error, info, off
```

To accept one occurrence, put `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=MDL405` on the line above it.
